questions.question: What symbol is used to mark an immediate value in AT&T syntax?
questions.explanation: In AT&T syntax, immediate values use $ prefix (e.g., $5, $100)
questions.title: Concept 01

questions.question: What symbol is used before register names in AT&T syntax?
questions.explanation: Registers use % prefix in AT&T syntax (e.g., %eax, %ebx)
questions.title: Concept 02

questions.question: What does the 'movl' instruction do?
questions.explanation: movl copies data from source to destination (movl source, dest)
questions.title: Concept 03

questions.question: What does the 'cmpl' instruction do?
questions.explanation: cmpl compares by subtracting first operand from second and setting flags
questions.title: Concept 04

questions.question: What does 'addl $5, %eax' do?
questions.explanation: addl adds the source ($5) to the destination (%eax)
questions.title: Concept 05

questions.question: What does 'jg' stand for?
questions.explanation: jg = Jump if Greater (used after cmpl for signed comparison)
questions.title: Concept 06

questions.question: What does 'je' stand for?
questions.explanation: je = Jump if Equal (also called jz - Jump if Zero)
questions.title: Concept 07

questions.question: What does 'jne' do?
questions.explanation: jne = Jump if Not Equal (also called jnz - Jump if Not Zero)
questions.title: Concept 08

questions.question: What does 'js' check for?
questions.explanation: js = Jump if Sign flag set (result is negative)
questions.title: Concept 09

questions.question: After 'cmpl $0, %eax', which instruction jumps if eax > 0?
questions.explanation: jg (Jump if Greater) jumps when the comparison shows greater than
questions.title: Concept 10

questions.question: Which is a valid 32-bit register in x86?
questions.explanation: %eax is the 32-bit accumulator register (e = extended)
questions.title: Concept 11

questions.question: What does %ebp typically point to?
questions.explanation: %ebp is the base pointer, used to access stack variables
questions.title: Concept 12

questions.question: What does '(%edx)' mean in AT&T syntax?
questions.explanation: Parentheses mean 'memory at address stored in register' (register indirect)
questions.title: Concept 13

questions.question: What does '-4(%ebp)' access?
questions.explanation: This is base+displacement addressing: memory at address (ebp - 4)
questions.title: Concept 14

questions.question: What does leal A, %eax load?
questions.explanation: lea computes the address of its memory operand; it does not read the value at that address.
questions.title: Concept 15

questions.question: What does 'subl $1, %eax' do?
questions.explanation: subl subtracts source from destination: eax = eax - 1
questions.title: Concept 16

questions.question: What does 'imull $2, %ebx' do?
questions.explanation: imull multiplies destination by source: ebx = ebx * 2
questions.title: Concept 17

questions.question: What does 'jmp' do?
questions.explanation: jmp always jumps to the specified label (unconditional)
questions.title: Concept 18

questions.question: In 'movl %eax, %ebx', which is the source?
questions.explanation: In AT&T syntax: instruction source, destination (opposite of Intel syntax)
questions.title: Concept 19

questions.question: How do you mark a label in assembly?
questions.explanation: Labels end with a colon: loop_start:, end_if:, etc.
questions.title: Concept 20

questions.question: Which instruction would you use for 'A = A + B'?
questions.explanation: addl adds values: addl %ebx, %eax (if eax=A, ebx=B)
questions.title: Concept 21

questions.question: What does 'movl $10, A' do?
questions.explanation: This stores the immediate value 10 into memory location A
questions.title: Concept 22

questions.question: After cmpl $0, %eax, which jump enters a loop body when signed eax > 0?
questions.explanation: jg takes the branch when ZF = 0 and SF = OF. An inverse jle branch can instead exit the loop.
questions.title: Concept 23

questions.question: What does 'jl' check for after a comparison?
questions.explanation: jl = Jump if Less than (signed comparison)
questions.title: Concept 24

questions.question: What happens to the operands after 'cmpl'?
questions.explanation: cmpl only sets flags for conditional jumps, doesn't modify operands
questions.title: Concept 25

questions.question: What does the 'l' suffix in 'movl' indicate?
questions.explanation: l = long (32-bit). Other suffixes: b=byte, w=word, q=quad
questions.title: Concept 26

questions.question: Which addressing mode is 'movl A, %eax'?
questions.explanation: This is direct addressing - accessing memory location by name (A)
questions.title: Concept 27

questions.question: Which addressing mode is 'movl (%edx), %eax'?
questions.explanation: Register indirect - edx contains an address, () dereferences it
questions.title: Concept 28

questions.question: To translate 'if(A == 0)', which instruction compares?
questions.explanation: cmpl compares A (in eax) with 0, then use je to jump if equal
questions.title: Concept 29

questions.question: After 'cmpl $5, %eax', when does 'je' jump?
questions.explanation: je (Jump if Equal) jumps when the comparison shows equality
questions.title: Concept 30
Concept 31
questions.question: Are movb and movl interchangeable?
options: No: movb moves 8 bits; movl moves 32 bits
questions.explanation: Operand size changes the operation. This practice interpreter supports only 32-bit instructions.

questions.title: Concept 32
questions.question: When does jne take its branch?
questions.explanation: jne/jnz branches when the Zero Flag is clear. Equality sets ZF, so jne does not jump on equality.

questions.title: Concept 33
questions.question: What signed condition does jge mean after cmp?
questions.explanation: jge tests SF = OF: signed greater than or equal. jle means less than or equal.

questions.title: Concept 34
questions.question: With edx = 4096 and ecx = 2, what address does 4(%edx,%ecx,4) use?
questions.explanation: Effective address = displacement + base + index × scale = 4 + 4096 + 2 × 4 = 4108.
